0.headline: NSE IPO GMP sees marginal decline ahead of issue launch on Thursday
0.heading: NSE IPO GMP sees marginal decline ahead of issue launch on Thursday
0.intro: NSE has seen an impact on its bottom line from reduced derivative trading volumes.
0.body:
The grey market premium (GMP) for the National Stock Exchange (NSE) IPO has seen a marginal decline ahead of the issue launch on Thursday, amid investor caution over the outlook for capital market firms due to declining derivatives trading volumes.

According to platforms tracking grey market activity, NSE shares are commanding a GMP of around 8-9 per cent in the unofficial market. Investorgain quoted a GMP of Rs 152 for NSE shares, indicating a listing gain of 8.52 percent. IPO Watch, meanwhile, quoted a GMP of 8.96 percent.

Earlier last week, the NSE IPO was commanding a GMP of more than 12 percent.

Reuters reported that investors are reluctant to pay higher prices due to regulatory changes that have slowed growth in options trading and an overhaul of trading rules to align Indian markets with global standards.

The NSE gets 80 percent of its revenue from trading, of which 60 percent comes from options trading. These volumes have dropped 27 percent from their peak in 2024, Reuters reported.

"NSE's high exposure to derivatives is a double-edged sword. Its dominant liquidity pool and scale are clear competitive strengths, but they also make earnings more sensitive to regulatory changes and shifts in trading activity," Gary Tan, portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments, told Reuters.

The NSE has also seen an impact on its bottom line from reduced derivative trading volumes. Its revenue from operations fell 3.1 percent in the fiscal year ended March 2026, while profit declined 15.5 percent.

According to Bernstein, Indian equity derivatives volumes are entering a phase of normalisation, with growth expected to slow to about 5 percent in the fiscal year ending 2027 due to regulatory measures on options trading.

(With inputs from Reuters)

1.headline: Manika Plastech IPO subscribed over 10x so far on final day; GMP drops to 7%
1.heading: Manika Plastech IPO subscribed over 10x so far on final day; GMP drops to 7%
1.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of plastic products manufacturing company Manika Plastech remained in demand on the final day of bidding, with the issue receiving 10.5 times subscription, as of 11:40 am on September 16, as per NSE data.
1.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of plastic products manufacturing company Manika Plastech remained in demand on the final day of bidding, with the issue receiving 10.5 times subscription, as of 11:40 am on September 16, as per NSE data.

Investors placed bids for 22,60,40,964 equity shares against 2,13,86,919 shares on offer. The retail investor portion was subscribed 14.43 times, while the non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 14.21 times.

The Rs 125.5-crore IPO will close today, on September 16. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 40-43 per share.

Read Also: SS Retail IPO booked 30% so far on Day 1; GMP at 30%

In the grey market, Manika Plastech shares were commanding a premium of 7 percent over the upper price band of Rs 43 on September 16, as per InvestorGain. Grey market premiums are unofficial indicators and can change before listing.

Ahead of the IPO opening, Manika Plastech raised Rs 37.6 crore from four anchor investors. The company said in an exchange filing on Thursday that it allotted 87.55 lakh equity shares to anchor investors at Rs 43 per share, the upper end of the price band.

The Wealth Company Alternates Trust-Bharat Value Fund-Series III, owned by Wealth Company Asset Management, a subsidiary of Pantomath Group, emerged as the largest anchor investor. It acquired 41.04 lakh shares for around Rs 17.6 crore.

Trust Mutual Fund, through two schemes, picked up 23.26 lakh shares worth around Rs 10 crore. Finavenue Capital Trust, through Finavenue Growth Fund, and Nova Global Opportunities Fund PCC, through Touchstone, invested Rs 5 crore each.

The Rs 125.5-crore issue comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 92.5 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 76.74 lakh shares by promoter entity VRIDAA Holding Trust, valued at around Rs 33 crore at the upper price band.

Of the fresh issue proceeds, the company plans to spend Rs 54.9 crore on capital expenditure for purchasing plant and machinery. Another Rs 15 crore will be used for repayment of debt, with the balance earmarked for general corporate purposes.

Check IPO News Here

The company operates seven manufacturing facilities with an installed capacity of 29,200 metric tonnes per annum (MTPA). Manika Plastech reported revenue of Rs 436 crore for the financial year ended March 2026, compared with Rs 406.5 crore a year earlier, representing growth of 7.3%. Its profit rose 15.9% to Rs 22.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 19.3 crore in FY25.

For the quarter ended June 2026, the company reported revenue of Rs 162.4 crore and profit of Rs 13 crore. Pantomath Capital Advisors is the merchant banker to the issue.

About Manika Plastech

Manika Plastech manufactures precision-engineered rigid polymer packaging products, including battery casings, pails and thin-wall containers. Its products are used across sectors such as automotive, energy storage, telecommunications, paints, lubricants, agrochemicals, construction chemicals, food and dairy.

2.headline: SS Retail IPO booked 30% so far on Day 1; GMP at 30%
2.heading: SS Retail IPO booked 30% so far on Day 1; GMP at 30%
2.intro: Multi-brand mobile retail chain SS Retail opened its initial public offering (IPO) today, with the issue receiving 30 percent subscription, as of 11:00 am on September 16, according to NSE data.
2.body:
Multi-brand mobile retail chain SS Retail opened its initial public offering (IPO) today, with the issue receiving 30 percent subscription, as of 11:00 am on September 16, according to NSE data.

The Rs 500-crore IPO received bids for 26,84,080 shares against 87,93,884 shares on offer. The retail investor portion was subscribed 52 percent, while the non-institutional investor (NII) category was booked 26 percent.

In the grey market, SS Retail shares were commanding a premium of around 30 percent over the upper end of the IPO price band, according to InvestorGain. Investors must note that the grey market premiums are unofficial indicators and can change before listing.

Read Also: Glass Wall Systems shares list at 7% premium over IPO price on NSE; should you buy, sell or hold?

The Rs 500-crore IPO will remain open for subscription until September 18. The issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 360 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of Rs 140 crore. The price band has been fixed at Rs 403-424 per share.

Ahead of the public issue, SS Retail raised Rs 146.4 crore from anchor investors through the allotment of 34.52 lakh shares to 14 institutional investors at Rs 424 per share.

Domestic mutual funds accounted for a significant portion of the anchor allocation. SS Retail allotted 28.70 lakh shares, or 83.14 percent of the total anchor book, to 11 domestic mutual funds through 19 schemes.

The investors included SBI Mutual Fund, Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company, Axis Mutual Fund, WhiteOak Capital, Motilal Oswal Asset Management Company, Invesco and Aditya Birla Sun Life Asset Management Company.

Bengal Finance and Investment, backed by investor Ashish Kacholia, Kotak Mahindra Life Insurance and 360 ONE were also among the anchor investors. The three investors collectively invested nearly Rs 25 crore in the issue.

SS Retail plans to use a substantial portion of the fresh issue proceeds towards funding its working capital requirements.

Of the net proceeds from the fresh issue, Rs 241.3 crore has been earmarked for incremental working capital requirements, while Rs 12.4 crore will be used for setting up new stores during the current financial year and FY28. The remaining funds will be deployed towards general corporate purposes.

The company plans to add 120 stores each in FY27 and FY28. Between April and July 2026, SS Retail had already added 33 stores.

For the planned store expansion, the company intends to spend up to Rs 5.81 crore on 57 stores in FY27 and up to Rs 6.64 crore on 58 stores in FY28.

SS Retail operates a multi-brand retail chain selling mobile phones, accessories and other electronic products. Its operations span Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Goa and Gujarat.

Check IPO News Here

As of July 31, 2026, the company had expanded its retail network to 536 stores across these five states. As of March 31, 2026, it operated 503 stores.

The company has a presence across metro, mini-metro, Tier-I, Tier-II and Tier-III and beyond cities, with a focus on smaller markets.

The IPO is being managed by Anand Rathi Advisors and Emkay Global Financial Services as the book-running lead managers. SS Retail's shares are scheduled to be listed on the NSE and BSE on September 23, subject to the completion of the IPO process.
